headline: A buyer is walking 355 Comanche RIGHT NOW at 1:15 — the first one through since the offer died Friday — and your seller still has not been told the offer is dead · DO: call Seth B. today, lead with the showing · WATCH: the fleet went dark 26 hours (Sat 9:18a → Sun 11:03a) and this board is the first read since.

notes: 🛑 THE FLEET WENT DARK FOR TWENTY-SIX HOURS AND NOTHING REPORTED IT. The heartbeat file has exactly TWO entries between Saturday 9:18 AM and right now: the Delta's pass 1 on Saturday morning, and the milestone engine at 11:03 this morning. In between — nothing. No Saturday Deep Dive, no Saturday afternoon or evening Delta passes, no Sunday letter, no console refresh since Saturday 7:55 AM. This is the known desktop-app-closed failure mode, not a broken routine: no BLOCKED lines exist because nothing ran to write one. Everything on this board older than 11:03 AM today was assembled by hand from primary sources this run.

⚠️ WHAT THE DARK WINDOW ACTUALLY COST, NAMED RATHER THAN GUESSED: three inbound home-value leads landed unanswered (Saturday 1:03 PM, Saturday 9:06 PM, and 2:27 AM this morning), and the Brivity instant-lead alert scenario has now been DEACTIVATED SINCE FRIDAY 9:32 AM — going on three days. That is the responder's only input and the first rung of the ownership check. Every lead that arrived this weekend arrived to silence.

✅ THE ONE ROUTINE THAT DID FIRE, FIRED WELL. The milestone engine woke at 11:03, scanned the full 27-hour gap across 26 listings, and caught the thing that mattered — 355 Comanche picking up a showing for today. It also correctly declined three non-events rather than inventing milestones. The 195 Lake View contract and the 5167 septic booking were both seen and both correctly judged below their rungs.

callBlock.who: Seth B. — a buyer is in his house at 1:15 today and he still doesn't know the offer died
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE ONE CALL WITH A CLOCK ON IT, AND THE CLOCK IS RIGHT NOW. A showing was confirmed Saturday 4:44 PM for TODAY 1:15–1:30 — Angela B. of Keller Williams Realty Vestavia, her first look at the house, the twelfth showing in its life. The MLS line on the notice reads $299,000 ACTIVE. ⭐ THAT TURNS THIS CALL FROM AN APOLOGY INTO AN UPDATE, which is why it leads the board. 🔴 THE OWED PART IS OLDER AND WORSE: you ruled the Cox/Lamp offer dead Saturday 7:55 AM, and no receipt on any lane shows your seller being told. He asked you directly on 7/28 — "No feedback from our counter?" — and that question has never been answered. ⭐ SO THE ORDER MATTERS: a buyer is in your house right now, then the offer is dead, then the listing is still working. Their buyers were papered at exactly $280,000 with no ceiling left; that is a buyer who ran out of room, not a failed negotiation. ⚠️ DO NOT QUOTE A COUNTER FIGURE — the machine holds two conflicting numbers and neither is clean. ⚠️ Set the pricing conversation up for later in the week; let today's read land first. A backup email is staged and unsent — send it after you dial, not instead.

Saturday 8:51 PM, in her own words: "I had asked to view a house in Mt Laurel tomorrow but I need to cancel." That single line settles what three routines could not — the 3:45 WAS today, Sunday, and the open house you referenced ending at three was the 2127 Hwy 93 one, not Fieldstone. ✅ AND YOU ALREADY HANDLED IT: at 10:24 this morning you wrote back "ok Do you have another day youd like to see it." Nothing is owed on the appointment. ⭐ WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE THING SHE ASKED FOR FOUR DAYS AGO. On 7/29 she pivoted to Mt Laurel, not much above $600,000, and you answered "will start working on that now — any must haves?" That question has been hanging since Wednesday and the Mt Laurel list has never gone out. She just cancelled a showing on a house she found herself; two or three real Mt Laurel options is what makes the rebook happen instead of waiting on her. ⚠️ Nobody has ever asked whether her own house has to sell first.

callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE CLEANEST AT-BAT ON THE BOARD AND IT IS BOTH SIDES OF A DEAL. Friday 5:02 PM, unprompted, off an automated listing alert: "We are very interested in this property! I think we are about ready to put ours on the market also! If you have time, we would love to get with you ASAP." ✅ You answered yourself at 5:33 and copied Darrell as she asked — "Sounds great and I will. Just let me know when ready and we will get busy!" ⚠️ BUT THAT REPLY PUTS THE NEXT MOVE ON HER AND SHE ASKED FOR THE OPPOSITE. She used the word ASAP and already said she's ready; a standing offer is not a calendar invite, and it is now two days old with nothing back. ⭐ THE CALL PROPOSES A SPECIFIC TIME and does both sides in one trip: walk the Helena house she flagged, then walk theirs. The buy side is the two-bathroom setup they told you in March they needed. ⚠️ CALL, DO NOT TEXT — the record shows Agent Referral as the source, so there is no consent trail for a text.

That was the cheap version; what's left is the honest version, which is a plain call about what he's actually hunting for. ⭐ Ownership was verified the hard way — read live in the leads index, not inferred from a webhook verdict — so this is genuinely yours. ⚠️ No text has gone out; his person page wedged when the sweep tried. He's inbound and gave the number, so a text is available if the call doesn't land.

callBlock.who: Virginia M. — past client, opened a listing alert at 10 PM Friday, and the CRM has never logged a single contact
callBlock.why: ⭐ TWO OPENS NINE DAYS APART IS A PATTERN, NOT A STRAY CLICK. Her record shows the alert sent and opened around 10 PM Friday, and the sweep logged another open twelve days before that. Four site visits, five listing views, average view price $323,000, and the CRM tags her intent as both seller and buyer. 🔴 THE PART THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU: last interaction reads NONE. The CRM has no logged contact with her ever — while Gmail shows you closed her purchase in June 2017 and checked in twice after, and her husband wrote back "give us a heads up when you're back this way and we can give you the tour." That invitation is eight years old and was never taken up. ⚠️ ONE FACT TO NOT GET WRONG ON THE CALL: her one transaction has been treated as a Birmingham address and it is not — it is a lake condo in a different county, so any equity number built off a Birmingham appreciation table is wrong for that asset. Ask, don't assert. ⚠️ The do-not-call flag on her record attaches to a third line only; mobile and home are clear.

callBlock.why: ⭐ THE BEST UNWORKED AT-BAT ON THE BOARD, AND THE TASK TEXT IS YOURS, NOT MACHINE NOISE — "Call!! Wants to discuss selling see notes," dated last December and roughly eight months overdue. ⚠️ A DEDUPE ACROSS BOTH ALIASES ON A 400-DAY WINDOW FOUND ZERO EMAILS TO HIM, EVER. The only activity on the record is your own note last November: "sent mailer." So the intent was logged, a mailer went out, and then eight months of nothing. ⚠️ TWO HONEST CAVEATS BEFORE YOU DIAL: the CRM has his intent as BUYER while your task says selling — one of the two is wrong and only the call settles it — and the property scores low to sell. This is an at-bat, not a layup. ⭐ But it is a free at-bat on a record that has never once been worked, and anything he told you in November may already have happened. No email was drafted deliberately: eight months of silence is a call, not a first email.
